sight.t: A low room, its corners lost past the reach of the light.
Everything here has been used for years and mended more than once.
A bed under a heap of blankets, a stool, a chest with an iron hasp.
Rushes on the floor, trodden flat along the path from door to hearth.
The hearth is banked; a red line of embers shows under the ash.
Wallpaper lifting at the seams, a clock on the mantel, a cold grate.
A couch, a television's dark screen, shoes kicked off by the door.
A wall screen showing nothing but the time, and a cleaning drone parked in its cradle.
A cup left half full, as if someone got up in a hurry.
A path worn in the floor, from the bed to the window.
The bedding has been slept in tonight; the dent is still there.
Scratches around the latch, fresh and bright against the old wood.
Something was hidden in the wall here once: the plaster is a shade newer in one place.

sound.t: The small noises of a house settling.
A draught finds a gap somewhere and whistles through it.
The fire ticks and shifts in the hearth.
Mice in the thatch.
A clock, loud in the quiet.
The hum of a refrigerator, and a tap that drips.
The building's air system, a low breath that never stops.
Someone in the next room turns over in bed.
Water drips into a bucket set under a leak.
A board creaks overhead, then nothing.
Breathing, slow and even, where nobody should be.

smell.t: Old smoke, worked into everything.
Damp wool and boiled food.
Tallow, and the animal fat it was made from.
The cowshed on the other side of the wall.
Coal dust and carbolic soap.
Cooking oil, laundry soap and stale cigarettes.
Filtered air, too clean, with a trace of plastic.
Bread baked this morning.
A chamber pot that wants emptying.
Herbs hung to dry above the bed: lavender, rue, something bitter.
Under the smoke, a trace of old blood that was scrubbed and scrubbed.

touch.t: The floor is gritty underfoot.
The air is close and warm near the hearth, cold by the walls.
The walls are wattle and daub, rough and dry to the touch.
The radiator is warm and ticks as it cools.
The table's edge is sticky with something spilled.
The latch is still warm from a hand.

sight.t: Tools hang on pegs, each in its own outline of dust.
A workbench scarred by years of use.
Shavings, offcuts and a half-finished piece clamped to the bench.
A forge, its coals grey, the anvil scaled with black.
Bolts of cloth stacked to the ceiling, and a counting board by the door.
Belts and pulleys run along the ceiling to the machines.
Fluorescent tubes, a time clock, a calendar from a supplier.
Fabrication units behind safety glass, status lights blinking amber.
One tool is missing from its place on the wall.
Work stopped in the middle: a measure drawn but not cut.
A ledger left open on the bench, the last entry blotted.
Marks on the floor where something heavy was dragged to the back.

sound.t: The building creaks as it cools.
Water drips into the quenching trough.
Hammering, steady, from somewhere close.
A machine idles somewhere, ticking.
A radio playing low, tuned between two stations.
The hum of servers and the click of a relay.
A cat moves among the stock.
Someone counting under their breath in the back room.

smell.t: Sawdust, sweat and lamp oil.
Coal smoke and hot iron.
Tanning: lime, dung and rot.
Dye vats, sour and sharp.
Machine oil and steam.
Solvent, coffee, burnt dust from a heater.
Ozone and the sweet smell of hot polymer.
Glue, freshly cooked.
Fresh blood under the sawdust, somebody's cut hand.

touch.t: Grit and shavings underfoot.
The forge still gives off a little heat.
The floor shakes faintly with a machine somewhere.
The bench is still warm where someone was leaning.

sight.t: Columns go up into a dark the light can't reach.
An altar under a white cloth, a cross above it.
Saints in paint and stone, their faces worn smooth by hands.
Rushlights by the altar; the nave beyond is black.
A single lamp burns before the sacrament.
Box pews with their little doors, and a high pulpit.
Gaslight in the side chapels, and plaques to the dead of the parish.
Electric candles in a rack, a coin box beside them.
Wax has dripped and hardened on the floor before one of the saints.
A prayer book left open on a bench.
A side door, not quite shut.
Dust lies thick everywhere except one path, to the crypt stair.
One of the floor slabs has been lifted and set back, the mortar broken.

sound.t: Every footstep comes back off the stone.
The building is so quiet the ears ring.
Monks at the night office, far off, a low chant.
A murmured prayer from one of the side chapels.
A pigeon shifts in the roof beams.
Someone breathing in the confessional.
A scrape of stone, under the floor.

smell.t: Cold stone and old incense.
Beeswax and dust.
Damp, and the smell of the graves under the floor.
Floor polish and lilies a few days old.
Smoke from a candle just snuffed.
Wet earth, carried in on someone's boots.
Under the incense, something dead and not long buried.

touch.t: The cold comes up from the stone floor.
The air moves very slowly, in long draughts.
The holy water stoup is dry.
The altar rail is worn smooth, and warm in one place.

sight.t: Carpets cover the floor, row on row, all facing the same wall.
A niche in the far wall marks the way to Mecca.
Shoes stand in pairs inside the door.
No pictures anywhere: bands of script run around the walls.
Oil lamps hang on long chains under the dome.
Gas brackets on the pillars, their glass gone yellow.
A ring of bulbs under the dome, and a cable running up to the minaret.
A Qur'an left open on its folding stand.
One carpet has been rolled back, and the floor under it scrubbed pale.
Footprints in the dust of the minaret stair go up and do not come down.

sound.t: Bare feet whisper over the carpets.
A voice reciting, low and steady, from a corner.
The call to prayer from the minaret, carried on the air.
The call to prayer, loud and crackling through a speaker.
Water running in the washing place off the court.
A whisper from the empty rows, too close.

smell.t: Old wool and rosewater.
Clean stone and the water of the washing place.
Lamp oil and a thread of incense.
Carpet cleaner and someone's cologne.
Dates and bread, set aside for after sunset.
Under the rosewater, old blood.

touch.t: The carpet is soft underfoot, and cool.
Cool air settles from the dome.
The floor before the niche is warm, as if someone knelt there a long while.

sight.t: Benches face a raised reading desk in the middle of the room.
A curtain hangs before the ark in the wall that faces Jerusalem.
A lamp burns over the ark; it is never let go out.
A gallery above, behind a wooden lattice.
Tallow candles in brass holders along the walls.
Gas jets in glass globes, and a board of donors' names.
Electric lights, and a camera over the street door.
A prayer shawl left folded on a bench.
The curtain of the ark hangs crooked, as if pulled aside in haste.
A name has been scratched off the memorial board, and not long ago.

sound.t: The wood creaks as the building settles.
Two voices from a side room, arguing over a text.
The street is close: carts and voices just beyond the wall.
A clock ticks somewhere in the gallery.
A page turns in the empty room.

smell.t: Old paper and candle wax.
Polished wood.
Wine and spice from the last blessing.
Damp, rising from the ritual bath below.
Smoke, though nothing here is burning.

touch.t: The benches are worn smooth by long use.
The room is cooler than the street.
The reading desk is warm under the hand.

sight.t: Incense smoke hangs in slow layers under the roof.
The holy images look down from the altar, gilded and calm.
Offerings on low tables: fruit, flowers, little heaps of rice.
Paper charms and strips of cloth hang from the beams.
Rows of small lamps flicker before the images.
Electric lamps shaped like lotus buds, and a box for coins.
One offering bowl has been knocked over and left where it fell.
The ash in the incense burner has been drawn into a shape.
The eyes of one image are wet.

sound.t: A bell struck once, and the hum that follows.
Chanting, many voices on one note.
Wind chimes in the eaves.
A drum, slow, from the back of the hall.
Beads clicking fast where nobody stands.

smell.t: Sandalwood and smoke.
Flowers left too long in the heat.
Rancid butter from the lamps.
Burnt sugar from the offerings.
Under the incense, something rotting.

touch.t: Stone or polished wood, cool under bare feet.
Warm air rises off the lamps.
A draught from behind the altar, where there should be a wall.

sight.t: Low beams, smoke, and tables crowded too close.
A fire in a wide hearth, and the regulars sitting nearest it.
Trestles and benches, ale in leather jacks and wooden cups.
The keeper's wife and daughter carry jugs between the tables.
Pewter tankards on hooks, a slate of what each drinker owes.
A long bar, a brass rail, gas mantles yellow with smoke.
A jukebox, a dartboard, a television over the bar showing the game.
Holographic menus over each table, and a bartender who never blinks.
Only a few tables still taken; the rest have their stools upturned.
Someone in the corner keeps their back to the wall and their eyes on the door.
A game of dice at the back, with more money on the table than it should have.
The keeper glances at the cellar door every so often.
One drinker hasn't touched the cup in front of them all night.

sound.t: Voices over each other, and somebody laughing too loud.
Cups set down hard, a bench scraping back.
A fiddle, badly tuned, and a few voices with it.
A piano, a song half the room knows.
Music from the jukebox, and the clack of pool balls.
A synth beat from the walls, and a dozen private calls at once.
The talk has dropped low; people lean in to speak.
Dice rattle at the back table and someone curses the throw.
Two people at the bar argue in whispers about money.
Upstairs, a floorboard creaks twice and stops.
A name, said very quietly, at the table by the door.

smell.t: Spilled ale, smoke and wet clothes drying by the fire.
Too many people in a small room.
Tallow, onions, a pot of something that has stewed since noon.
The rushes on the floor need changing.
Tobacco, gin and sawdust.
Beer, pipe smoke and paraffin.
Cigarettes, fryer oil, bleach in the toilets.
Synthetic tobacco, flavored vapour, and the sharp edge of a stimulant someone is smoking.
Someone has been sick out the back.
One of the drinkers smells of horse and the road; they have come a long way today.
Under the smoke, blood: a little, fresh.

touch.t: The heat of the fire on one side, the draught from the door on the other.
The floor is sticky.
The table is still wet from a spilled cup.

sight.t: A room that nobody lives in, by the look of it.
The windows have been covered, every one.
A crypt, or a cellar made into one: a long box on trestles.
Heavy curtains nailed at the edges, and dust on every surface.
Blackout blinds, a steel door, a mattress on the floor.
Nothing to eat or drink anywhere, and no sign there ever was.
The lock on the inside of the door is better than the one outside.
The dust has been disturbed only on one path, from the door to the resting place.

sound.t: Silence, close and heavy.
The door, when it moves, makes no sound at all: oiled hinges.
Rats, and then the rats go still.
Water dripping behind the walls.

smell.t: Cold, dry air, like a cellar in winter.
Dust, old wood, and nothing living.
Earth, as if the floor were bare ground under the boards.
Old blood, dried brown, faint but certain.
A trace of something sweet, like grave flowers left too long.

touch.t: The room is colder than it should be.
The air hasn't moved in a long time.
The resting place is cold, colder than the room.

sight.t: A heavy gate, and a smaller door cut into it for night traffic.
Arrow slits, and a brazier where the watch warm their hands.
Pikes in a rack, and a bench for the men off duty.
A watch-house lantern, and a table where papers are checked.
A sentry box, a barrier pole painted in stripes.
A checkpoint booth, floodlights, a barrier arm.
Scanning arches, a drone overhead, guards in visored helmets.
The gate is shut and barred; only the wicket opens.
One of the watch is asleep on their feet.
A notice nailed up by the door, with a description of someone wanted.
The bar on the gate is not seated all the way.

sound.t: A guard's boots on the walk above.
The watch talking about pay and the cold.
A watchman calls the hour.
A radio crackles in the booth.
Dice in the guardroom.
Someone outside the gate, waiting, shuffling their feet.

smell.t: Wood smoke from the brazier, wet leather, unwashed bodies.
Horse dung from the gate road.
Diesel exhaust and coffee.
Ale on a guard's breath.

touch.t: Wind funnels through the gate arch.
The stone of the gate is cold and wet.

sight.t: An open square, its paving uneven, a well or fountain at its heart.
Stalls, awnings, and people pushing between them.
The stalls are bare frames now; scraps blow across the stones.
A market cross, a pillory, the church tower over the roofs.
A weigh house with the town's scales, and a pump with a chained cup.
Gas lamps around the edge, carts with their shafts down.
Parked cars, a bus shelter, shop signs lit up.
Advertising screens on every surface, some flickering with dead pixels.
A cutpurse working the edges of the crowd.
A notice of a hanging, a few days old.
Someone watching the square from a window above the baker's.

sound.t: The square throws noise back from every side.
Traders crying their goods, a cart wheel squealing.
A dog barks, and another answers it from across the town.
Geese, a pig squealing, a bell for the market's opening.
Traffic, a busker, a car alarm somewhere.
Water running in the fountain, or the well chain swinging.
Footsteps, behind and to one side, keeping pace.

smell.t: Trampled vegetables, horse dung, wet stone.
Bread, fish, spices and a hundred people.
The tannery downwind, and the butchers' shambles.
Coal smoke, horses and roasting chestnuts.
Exhaust fumes, hot fat from a food stall.
Rotting fruit in the gutter.
Smoke from a fire someone shouldn't have lit.

touch.t: The wind has room to move here.
The cobbles are slick.

sight.t: A narrow way between houses that lean toward each other overhead.
Doors shut, shutters closed, a gutter down the middle.
The upper floors jut out, nearly touching across the lane.
A lamp in a niche, a street sign painted on the wall.
Gas lamps at long intervals, pools of light and the dark between.
Streetlights, parked cars, a phone box.
Neon in a dozen scripts, and a security camera on every corner.
One window still lit, high up.
A gap between two houses, wide enough for one person.
Something has been dragged through the gutter here.
Someone standing in a doorway, keeping still.
Fresh chalk marks on a doorpost, a sign meant for someone.

sound.t: The echo of footsteps.
Water running in the gutter.
A shutter bangs somewhere in the wind.
The watch, far off, calling the hour.
A carriage passes in the next street.
A car goes by slowly, its radio up.
The whine of an aircar passing low.
Voices behind a shutter, a quarrel.
Footsteps behind, stopping when you stop.

smell.t: The gutter, and what has been thrown in it.
Wet stone and chimney smoke.
Night soil, pigs, and somebody's bread oven.
Coal smoke, horses, the river.
Exhaust, wet tarmac, a takeaway.
Hot wiring, rain on concrete, cheap noodle broth.
Cat piss in the doorways.
Lamp oil from a lamp just put out.

touch.t: The way underfoot is uneven and slick.
A cold wind down the length of the street.

sight.t: Thick walls, deep windows, tapestries against the cold.
A great hall with a high table at one end.
A hearth in the middle of the hall, its smoke going up to a hole in the roof.
Banners, shields on the walls, the lord's arms over the high seat.
Portraits in gilt frames, a long gallery, a staircase of oak.
Gas brackets on old stone, hunting trophies, a billiard table.
Velvet ropes and a sign for the gift shop; this part is a museum now.
The hall is dark; servants sleep on the benches along the walls.
A guard at the stair who looks at everyone who passes.
One tapestry hangs a little out from the wall.
Scuffs on the floor lead to a panel that isn't flush.

sound.t: Voices carry up the stair from the hall.
Dogs in the hall, scratching and settling.
A sentry on the wall walk, pacing.
A servant sweeping the rushes.
A door shuts somewhere above.
Someone talking low in the window seat.

smell.t: Wood smoke, dogs and roasting meat.
Cold stone and beeswax.
Rushes strewn with herbs to sweeten them.
Coal fires and furniture polish.
Wine, spilled and soaked into the boards.
The garderobe, at the end of the passage.

touch.t: The cold of the stone walls comes right through.
A draught from every arrow slit.

sight.t: Trees, close and dark, and the path between them.
Open fields, a hedge line, the black edge of a wood.
Nothing past a few yards but shapes.
Birds in the hedges, a hawk over the field.
A shrine at the crossroads, its offerings rotted.
A fence with a rusted sign, power lines on the hill.
Tracks in the mud, a few hours old.
Broken branches at shoulder height.
A trail heading off the path, used by something.
Bones scattered under a tree, too clean, too many.

sound.t: The wind in the trees.
A stream, somewhere below.
An owl, then quiet.
Birdsong starting, one bird and then dozens.
Something heavy moves in the undergrowth.
The woods go silent all at once.
A howl, far off, answered nearer.

smell.t: Leaf mould, wet earth, pine.
Grass and cattle.
Wood smoke from a fire somewhere ahead.
Carrion, faint, on the wind.
Wet fur, and the musk of a large animal.

touch.t: Wet grass soaks through to the ankles.
The wind comes across the open ground.
The ground is soft here; it gives underfoot.

sight.t: Standing stones, or a ring of old trees, at the centre of the place.
The grass grows differently here.
Small offerings in a hollow: feathers, teeth, a bit of bone.
Claw marks scored into the bark, higher than anyone could reach.
The moonlight falls more brightly here than it should.

sound.t: The air is quiet, as if waiting.
Water underground, running.
Wolves, somewhere close, and not hiding it.

smell.t: Earth, stone and growing things, very strong.
Wolf, all around.
Old ash from a great fire.

touch.t: The hairs on the arms stand up.
The ground hums, very faintly, or seems to.

sight.t: Nothing here stands out at first look.
Something has been moved recently; the dust shows it.
A detail that doesn't fit: a door where none should be, a mark on a wall.

sound.t: The usual noises of the place, and nothing more.
A sound from somewhere nearby, too faint to place.

smell.t: Dust, damp and people.
A trace of smoke.

touch.t: The air is still.
A draught from somewhere.
